liner.body_md:
## What listeners single out

- **Scarlet Begonias** (1 review, 1 other source): Reviewer calls the Scarlet Begonias into Fire On The Mountain pairing fantastic; Setlist shows Scarlet Begonias going into Fire On The Mountain, then back to Scarlet before Saint Of Circumstance [1][18]
- **Bird Song** (2 reviews): Reviewer calls Bird Song a high point of the first set; Reviewer suggests Bird Song and Box Of Rain may be the best performances [24][25]
- **Saint Of Circumstance** (2 reviews): Reviewer finds the Saint weak; Reviewer agrees the Saint is flubbed and is the show's weak spot [24][25]
- **Stagger Lee** (1 review): Reviewer singles out Stagger Lee as a standout [18]
- **They Love Each Other** (1 review): Reviewer notes Sugaree did not follow They Love Each Other, unusual for a while [22]
- **Little Red Rooster** (1 review): Reviewer finds Rooster strong, with Brent's rasping vocals working well rather than combative [22]
- **Hell In A Bucket** (1 review): Opens a little loose but finishes with a raucous ending [22]

## Setlist highlights

- **gd89-04-16 t01 Crowd**: earliest performance in the archive; legendary: the only archived performance [29]
- **gd89-04-16 t02 Hell In A Bucket**: earliest performance in the archive; legendary: the only archived performance [29]
- **gd89-04-16 t03 They Love Each Other**: earliest performance in the archive; legendary: the only archived performance [29]
- **gd89-04-16 t04 Little Red Rooster**: earliest performance in the archive; legendary: the only archived performance [29]
- **gd89-04-16 t05 Stagger Lee**: earliest performance in the archive; legendary: the only archived performance [29]
- **gd89-04-16 t06 Mama Tried**: earliest performance in the archive; legendary: the only archived performance [29]
- **gd89-04-16 t07 Mexicali Blues**: earliest performance in the archive; legendary: the only archived performance [29]
- **gd89-04-16 t08 Bird Song**: earliest performance in the archive; legendary: the only archived performance [29]

## The recordings

- **gd1989-04-16.140995.schoeps.cmc4.mk4.pcm.mattes.miller.clugston.flac1644** (recommended): audience recording; 21 songs; 142 min [1]
- **gd1989-04-16.167825.mtx.seamons.ht169.flac16**: matrix (soundboard mixed with audience mics); 18 songs; 138 min; rated 5/5 by 1 [2]
- **gd1989-04-16.sbd.walker-scotton.miller.81703.sbeok.flac16**: soundboard; 18 songs; 137 min; rated 3.75/5 by 8 [4]. Said about its sound: Reviewer says this source sounds much better than the other source, and rates the sound four; Reviewer describes the audio quality of this version as superb and clear [24][25]
- **gd1989-04-16.149699.UltraMatrix.sbd.cm.miller.flac16**: soundboard; 18 songs; 137 min [5]
- **gd1989-04-16.akg460b.volkerding.96081.flac16**: source not stated; 18 songs; 136 min; rated 3.5/5 by 2 [7]. Said about its sound: Accurate omni representation of how the show sounded; possibly good raw material for a multichannel mix [7]
- **gd89-04-16.sbd.sbefixed.9963.sbeok.shnf**: soundboard; 18 songs; 129 min; rated 4.38/5 by 8 [9]. Said about its sound: Reviewer recalls an earlier listen where the recording quality seemed poor, and wonders whether this fixed version improved it [17]

## Around the show

- Reviewer saw this show and remembers it fondly, calling the venue stellar [17]
- Reviewer had asked a companion to hear Saint Of Circumstance; the venue had a dance room with speakers and photos from Alpine [23]
- Attendee sat second row in front of Phil at the Mecca on both nights [26]
- Reviewer says Weir belts his lyrics with crunchy guitar fills, and Brent lifts the band whenever it drags [27]
- A screaming man during Drums, Space, The Other One and Stella Blue was removed by security [7]
- Reviewer ranks the 17 July show as the best of the five Wisconsin shows in 1989 [18]
- Described as short but solid like the previous night; this source sounds a bit better than that night's [20]
- Reviewer considers it one of the best shows of Spring 1989 [21]
- Reviewer saw 7 or 8 shows on the tour and thinks the two Milwaukee shows were the tightest and hottest [27]

## Tapers and lineage

- **gd1989-04-16.140995.schoeps.cmc4.mk4.pcm.mattes.miller.clugston.flac1644**: taped by Ted Mattes; transferred by Scott Clugston and Charlie Miller; source: Source Info: Ted Mattes' Master Audience PCM (Nakamichi DMP-100 deck); Schoeps CMC4/MK4 mics, ortf (OTS); Transfer Info: Master PCM (Sony SL-10)> Sony PCM… [1]
- **gd1989-04-16.167825.mtx.seamons.ht169.flac16**: source: Matrix by Hunter Seamons using Final Cut Pro (FLAC > AIFF > Final Cut > Soundtrack Pro > AIFF CD tracking via Audacity > FLAC16 via xACT w/meta-tagging) June… [2]. Also: Matrix of soundboard and audience tape; the soundboard ran slow in both sets and was pitch corrected; Used the older Scotton and Walker soundboard over a newer Pearson one; Scarlet > Fire patched from another source [2]
- **gd1989-04-16.sbd.walker-scotton.miller.81703.sbeok.flac16**: transferred by Charlie Miller; source: SBD -> Cassette Master (TDK MA-XG90) D [4]
- **gd1989-04-16.149699.UltraMatrix.sbd.cm.miller.flac16**: taped by Don Pearson and Dan Healy; transferred by All Transfers and Mastering by Charlie Miller  April 20, 2020; source: UltraMatrix SBD > Cassette Master (TDK MA-X90) [5]
- **gd1989-04-16.akg460b.volkerding.96081.flac16**: taped by Pat Volkerding; transferred by Pat Volkerding; source: Source: AKG 460B omni capsules, 7' high, 6' spread > Crown phantom power > Sony TC-D5M (pass-thru) > Yamaha MT1X (dbx type II encode, Maxell XL-IIS) [7]. Also: Taper's only omni recording, made with AKG mics; phantom power lost twice during Mexicali Blues, and silences were clipped out [7]
- **gd89-04-16.sbd.sbefixed.9963.sbeok.shnf**: source: Shntool fix by Willy of previous Braverman seed [9]

## Art and photos

- Fan art by Kirsten Michel: [1989-04-16 The MECCA, Milwaukee, WI, USA - Jerry Garcia](https://jerrygarcia.com/show/1989-04-16-the-mecca-milwaukee-wi-usa/) [30]

Reviewer finds the Saint weak

Reviewer describes the audio quality of this version as superb and clear

Attendee sat second row in front of Phil at the Mecca on both nights
Reviewer saw 7 or 8 shows on the tour and thinks the two Milwaukee shows were the tightest and hottest
